newsitem.title: USA: Cuyahoga County, Ohio, treasurer to retire.
newsitem.headline: Cuyahoga County, Ohio, treasurer to retire.

text.p: Cuyahoga County Treasurer Francis Gaul, 70, whose appeal of his conviction for dereliction of duty is still pending, said Tuesday he will retire March 1.
His term was to end in September.
Gaul, who has been treasurer since 1975, headed the office when a controversial investment fund run by his office was shut down in 1994.

The SAFE, or Secured Assets Fund Earnings fund, which once contained more than $1 billion in assets, lost about $114 million when it was shut down after revelations of large paper losses, risky investment strategies and leveraging.
Gaul was convicted of dereliction of duty, a misdemeanor, in connection with the fund, but has appealed the conviction.
Another treasurer's office employee pleaded guilty to similar charges.
In addition, the county filed a civil suit seeking unspecified damages from brokers who sold investments to the fund.
Gaul, who did not stand for re-election last fall, was to remain in office until September, when the new treasurer's term normally begins.
Gaul said in a telephone interview that this is a logical time for him to step down because the county's six-month tax collection cycle has just ended.

In addition, property reappraisals that will be done in 1997 require the treasurer maintain a "close working relationship" with other county officials and he wanted to give Rokakis time to develop that.

Former Cleveland city councilman James Rokakis, who was elected to succeed Gaul in September, now is likely to step into the post early, county administrator Tom Hayes said in a telephone interview. Rokakis is a lawyer.
